A month ago, I attended the Locus (YC F25) Agentic Payments Hackathon at the Y Combinator office in SF and won 2nd place for Stripe 's prize track with my teammates Mukund P. , ESHAN CHAWLA , and Uday Arora ! Never thought I'd make it to such an incredible event, but one application on a Monday afternoon made it all possible. I didn't even know who I was going to work with, but I met my teammates the morning of the event and got along through vibes. In just an hour, we decided to address a logistical problem many of our friends and family members face at work: navigating corporate travel for conferences, company off-sites, and similar work-related events. Our platform, TripWeaver was built to simplify and customize the tedious sequence of booking flights, hotels, and ride-share/rental car services for each individual within a business team. We utilized Anthropic 's SDK to connect our agent to the Kiwi.com MCP server to obtain the latest flight and travel info. We pitched our project as one of the last teams to do so for Stripe , and they loved it! We won 2nd place and were given awesome prizes such as: - $2k in processing credits - free merch - and a visit to the Stripe office in South SF! Thank you Mark Moriarty and Peter Masone for the valuable feedback on our project and for inviting us to lunch at the office this past week! Additionally, thank you Cole Dermott , Eliot Lee , and the Locus (YC F25) team for organizing such an impactful 1-day event! ...more

Incredibly excited to share that our team won 2nd Place at the Locus (YC F25) Agentic Payments hackathon at the Y Combinator office in San Francisco this weekend! 🥈 This was the first hackathon I've participated in here in the US since starting my Master's, and the energy was amazing. What's even wilder is that my teammates Uday Arora , Surya Pugazhenthi and Mukund P met for the first time at the event and managed to build this in just one day. The Problem: Corporate travel (for sales teams, conferences, sponsored events, company off sites, etc.) is a huge logistical headache. It's a manual mess of booking, endless reimbursements, and juggling individual preferences. Our Solution: We built an AI agent to automate and personalize this process at scale. Using the Anthropic SDK, our agent connects to the Kiwi MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server to pull real-time flight and travel data. Here's the magic: An organizer just sets a budget and adds the attendees. The agent instantly generates a full itinerary (flights, stays) for everyone, personalised to their known preferences. Crucially, it then individually chats with each attendee to make adjustments ("Can I get a later flight?") before automatically booking everything, all while staying within the original budget constraints. This moves corporate travel from a manual chore to a scalable, automated, and personalised experience. We’re so grateful for the recognition and the prize! --> $2,000 in Stripe credits --> A team lunch at Stripe HQ --> Awesome SWAG! And a special thank you to the judges Mark Moriarty and Brendan Ryan for their time and insightful feedback ! A massive thank you to the organisers at Y Combinator , Locus (YC F25) , Stripe , and Anthropic for supporting such a great event! #Hackathon #YC #SanFrancisco #AI #Stripe #Anthropic #MCP #AIagent #CorporateTravel #MSinAI #SJSU ...more ...more

Last month, I had the honor of taking home two awards at University of California, Santa Cruz events on back-to-back weekends! 🎉 🏆 CruzHacks – BenefitFinder: Best Beginner Hack Project CruzHacks was our very first hackathon for our entire team. We dove in together, learned on the fly, and delivered a project we're proud of. BenefitFinder is a web app that helps users quickly discover government and non-profit benefits tailored to their needs. By entering a few basic details, our platform matches people to programs like scholarships, financial aid grants, and more—making life-changing resources more accessible to everyone. I focused on building the backend services and integrating our eligibility-rules engine to ensure a seamless, beginner-friendly experience. We’re also excited to have been invited to showcase BenefitFinder at an exclusive event early next month—more info coming soon in an updated post! Thank you to the greatest hackathon team I could ever have for a first-time experience: Glenn Grant-Richards , Max Ratcliff , and Alexis Valdes View our submission here: https://lnkd.in/gx_9gJ6F Try BenefitFinder here: https://lnkd.in/gZKyYbFJ 🎨 Google Developer Group On Campus at UCSC – slugspace: Best UI/UX slugspace is our roommate-matching mobile app for UCSC students that mimics popular dating apps such as Tinder and Hinge to deliver lightning-fast, dynamic swiping and filters—letting students find the perfect roommate match based on lifestyle choices, roommate preferences, and more. I led the UI/UX design, crafting intuitive filter controls and responsive layouts so that browsing potential roommates feels effortless. Glenn Grant-Richards and I will work on transforming slugspace this summer into a larger platform that integrates with almost any university, not just UCSC. Housing selection will be added to cover the full roommate-housing search experience. We are aiming to release on the app store around mid-summer to ensure students have enough time to find roommates and close in their housing options before the start of the next school year in the fall. Thank you Team #23 for pulling through with slugspace until the end and seeing our once-silly idea into a working demo app: Glenn Grant-Richards , Angad Pantvaidya , Nidhi Sunil , and Yash Khot No app release yet, but you can view the project on GitHub here: https://lnkd.in/gqN7nbPt A huge thank-you to the organizers of both CruzHacks and Google Developer Group On Campus at UCSC for arranging these incredible events, and to all of my amazing teammates—your intuition and hard work made these wins possible. 🙌 Looking forward to continuing to build these projects and tackling my next one. If you’re curious to learn more about BenefitFinder, slugspace, or just want to chat about turning projects into entry-level products, let’s connect! ...more

Un-retired from hackathons to come back and win Grokathon, hosted by xAI the bet we made was that AI is finally smart enough to reverse engineer from raw binary if you hand it the right tools so we gave Grok Build a ghidra mcp to read the disassembly, an emulator it could poke memory in, and a screen + controller so it could actually play the game first test: Breakout, a 33kb GameBoy ROM 15 minutes later, a frame for frame reconstruction in clean C then we launched it publicly and people competed for leaderboard spots 2500+ views, 750 game runs, 150 users from there, people started asking for custom versions, so we made remixing a feature: tag us on X with a request ("make it fire themed") and our harness spins up in a sandbox, changes the code, and posts it to the arcade then we went 8x bigger: Kirby's Dream Land, 262kb which took 90+ minutes but it eventually got it done and to push the harness to its limit, we reverse engineered a 1995 BMW engine control unit and reconstructed its runtime from just the binary check it out: https://lnkd.in/gkfSH3VY shoutout to my cracked teammates Theo Chapman and Henry Zhang along with Umesh Khanna and Ishan Deshpande for hosting

Ben Horowitz on how a game studio turned it's last $6 million into Slack : "Stewart calls me. He says, 'Ben, I've got $6 million left. I have no way to raise money because I've made really no progress. So I've got three choices. I can pray for rain and try and finish it, I can shut down the company and give you your $6 million back, or we built this tool that we use in our engineering team to communicate with each other, and I could just put that out as a product.'" "I'm like, 'What? You just built some tool to talk to each other and you want to put that out as a product? And you're a consumer guy, and you want to become an enterprise software guy?'" "$6 million is not gonna make any difference in my life. If you really think it's a good idea, go ahead." Ben Horowitz Talks Honesty, Failure, and Secrets at UC Berkeley (2016)
